source.section: Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8; Line 10b, Instructions PDF page 8 and Form IL-1040 PDF page 1

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 248,850.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 1,150.00 = 250,000.00. Federal taxable income = 250,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - additional amount for 1 person(s) 65 or older 2,000.00 = 232,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 250,000.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 250,000.00. Line 5 IRA distribution 1,150.00 = 1,150.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 1,150.00. Line 9 base income = 250,000.00 - 1,150.00 = 248,850.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 250,000.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 1,000.00 (1 box(es) x 1,000.00). Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 3,850.00. Line 11 net income = 248,850.00 - 3,850.00 = 245,000.00. Line 12 tax = 245,000.00 x 4.95% = 12,127.5000. The form takes whole dollars only and would show 12,128.00; expected uses the formula to the cent. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 12,127.50. The printed word is 'greater than', so federal AGI of exactly 250,000.00 keeps both amounts.
